thread_analysis.thread_summary: Elematec Corporation (contacts Daiki Kobayashi, then primarily Yuichiro Shouwaki from the Kumagaya branch) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida) in an extended, FAQ-rich pre-registration consulting engagement for a Bluetooth-enabled smart tracker (Tag and Card variants), spanning December 2024 through January 2026 -- the longest single engagement period and largest thread in this batch. The thread is exceptionally dense with foundational, broadly-applicable Bluetooth SIG and adjacent Japan Radio Law (Giteki) regulatory questions, reflecting a customer new to both regimes working through corporate-structure complexities (parent/subsidiary brand and membership identity), before the engagement concludes with an actual registration quote in late 2025/early 2026 under the newly-effective QPRDv4 framework.
all_questions_found: Can a non-SIG-member brand owner have registration filed on their behalf by a SIG-member manufacturing subcontractor? (see thread_0032_case_01)
What real-world enforcement risk exists for selling uncertified Bluetooth products, and has any company actually been sued? (see thread_0032_case_02)
Does Japan Radio Law's module-reuse certification exemption apply to a bare chip, and does it cover OEM/ODM rebranded products? (see thread_0032_case_03)
Must the registered model name exactly match the actual store-sold product, and how does SIG actually verify this? (see thread_0032_case_04)
How does the Product List mechanism work for multiple SKU variants under one Declaration ID, and can a registered name be corrected? (see thread_0032_case_05)
What are BRTF and BQTF fees, and are they relevant to an ordinary customer's registration cost? (see thread_0032_case_06)

Which company's name (parent vs. subsidiary) determines SIG registration obligation when brand trademark and selling entity differ, and what's the Japan Radio Law small-device packaging display exception? (see thread_0032_case_07)
What Bluetooth Brand Guide trademark footnote and company-name display rules apply when referencing SIG membership or the Bluetooth name/logo? (see thread_0032_case_08)
What are the practical mechanics of SIG membership application (parent/subsidiary independence, domain ownership proof, registrant eligibility)? (see thread_0032_case_09)
Does SIG distinguish member companies by email domain, and what happens when a parent and subsidiary share one? (see thread_0032_case_10)

(Administrative/anecdotal, not separately cased) Speculative discussion of why some products (e.g., Nintendo Wii, BLE-only trackers) omit Bluetooth logo display despite being properly certified; standard registration timeline estimates (3 business days with no testing vs. 6+ weeks with profile testing) and Invoice address-rewriting procedure for proxy wire transfers; final-stage registration quote reflecting the QPRDv4 (effective July 2025) reclassification of the customer's two products' registration methods -- consistent with already-documented post-2024 system mechanics.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread is the most comprehensive single source in this batch for foundational SIG membership and registration-identity rules: the selling-company-must-itself-be-a-member principle (case_01), the parent/subsidiary nameplate and email-domain identity rules (case_07, case_10), and the Bluetooth Brand Guide's trademark display requirements (case_08) collectively form a near-complete picture of corporate-structure considerations that aren't covered with this level of detail anywhere else in the corpus. Case_02's enforcement-mechanism and FCA litigation precedent, and case_06's BRTF/BQTF fee clarification, are similarly unique, high-value additions.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0032_case_01 through thread_0032_case_10 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_10 (shared email domain forcing internal-division treatment) carries particularly high risk of silently blocking an intended independent registration if not checked proactively, and case_07 (parent vs. subsidiary nameplate identity) risks registering the wrong corporate entity entirely.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant patiently worked through an unusually large volume of foundational questions from a customer new to both Bluetooth SIG and Japan Radio Law regimes, consistently distinguishing the two regulatory frameworks' different identity bases (nameplate company for both, but with different display mechanics) and flagging practical workarounds (placeholder model names, delete-and-re-add corrections, domain ownership proof generation) proactively.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer is new to Bluetooth SIG certification and has a multi-entity corporate structure (parent/subsidiary, brand trademark holder vs. operational seller), proactively walk through the nameplate-identity and email-domain-identity rules in detail before registration begins, since these can silently determine which entity must hold SIG membership and can block an intended registration path (e.g., shared email domains forcing internal-division treatment) in ways the customer would not anticipate from general intuition about which company is 'really' selling the product.
